references.text: Moses commands the people not to turn aside from the Lord's command to the right or to the left, the same instruction given in Deuteronomy 28:14.
The king shall not turn aside from the command, either to the right or to the left, a similar formulation regarding faithfulness to God's word.
Joshua is told not to turn aside from the law to the right or to the left, a direct parallel to the warning in Deuteronomy 28:14.
Joshua warns the people against following other gods and urges them to hold fast to the Lord's law without turning to either side.
A warning against letting the heart be led astray to worship other gods and serve them, addressing the same theme of apostasy.
A prohibition against following other gods, even if prophets perform signs, paralleling the warning against idolatry.
Words of wisdom about not turning aside to the right or to the left, but keeping away from evil.
The first commandment forbids having other gods and worshipping them, forming the basis for the warning in Deuteronomy 28:14.
Solomon's heart was turned toward other gods, an example of breaking the command not to follow foreign gods.
